threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, roles and initial household targeting approach.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the Community Food Support and Outreach Pilot. I've shared the overview in A1 which sets out our 6-week objective: to design and run a pilot combining surplus food redistribution with basic wellbeing checks for vulnerable households. The key deliverables are mapped processes, weekly schedules, outreach protocols, training, and a final report. Before we dive into operations, I'd like to align on scope and roles. Does everyone have clarity on what success looks like for this pilot? And should we start thinking about which households we want to reach?

Thanks for the overview. I've reviewed A1 and I'm clear on the scope. For household targeting, I think we should start with a smaller cohort—maybe 15-20 households in the first week to test our processes before scaling. We can work with local community organisations to pre-identify them. What's the team's thinking on eligibility criteria? Should we focus on age, isolation, or specific needs?

Good point on starting small. For eligibility, I'd suggest we keep it simple: households with at least one adult aged 65+, or those flagged by community partners as isolated or in food insecurity. We avoid clinical assessments—that's not our role. I'll draft the criteria and share with community partners for feedback. Does that direction work for everyone?

That sounds reasonable. I'm thinking about the practical side—once we have the household list, we'll need to organise how we collect and sort the food. Should we be thinking about that in parallel, or wait until we've confirmed the households first?

We can start planning the collection and sorting process now—it doesn't depend on the household list. I'll draft a step-by-step process for receiving surplus food, checking it against food safety rules, and packing it. That's T2. I'll need to align with the shelf filler team on feasibility and then get it reviewed before we move forward.

While you're working on that, I can start mapping the delivery routes. I'll need the household list and the weekly packing schedule to finalise the routes, but I can do a draft based on the geography we know. That's T4. Once we have the households confirmed, I can optimise and check feasibility against our current delivery workload.

Perfect. So the sequence is: confirm households and eligibility (D2), then operations can move forward with collection, packing and routes. Let me also confirm—are we all aligned that the pilot objective is to reach 15-20 households over 6 weeks, with weekly deliveries and brief wellbeing checks at the door? That's D1. If yes, I'll document that as our success criteria.

Yes, that's clear. One thing I want to flag—we'll need to make sure the outreach part doesn't overwhelm the delivery staff. The script needs to be short and simple. I assume that's something we'll cover in the next thread?

Absolutely. That's T5—I'll draft a short doorstep script that's non-clinical and respectful. We'll review that in the safety and privacy thread. For now, let me confirm: D1 and D2 are locked in. I'll move forward with finalising the household list with community partners by end of week, and the team can start on their respective tasks. Sound good?

threads.thread_goal: Design and agree on the end-to-end operational flow from surplus collection to delivery.

messages.text: Hi all, I've drafted the collection and sorting process for T2. The flow is: receive surplus food, check expiry and condition, sort by type, store in designated areas following rotation rules, and pack into weekly parcels. I've aligned this with food safety guidance—we'll follow basic hygiene rules like hand washing, temperature checks, and clear labelling. The full process is in T2. I'd like feedback from the shelf filler team on whether this is feasible with our current storage and equipment.

I've reviewed the draft. The process looks solid, but I have a question on storage—do we have enough shelf space for a week's worth of surplus food for 15-20 households? We might need to stagger the collection or use the back storage area. Also, I think we should test the packing process with a sample run before we commit. That's part of T6.

Good catch on storage. Let's use the back area for overflow and rotate stock daily to avoid spoilage. For the packing test, I agree—let's do a sample run this week with 5 parcels and see how long it takes and what issues come up. I'll coordinate with you on timing. Once we've tested, we can finalise the process and move to D3.

While you're testing packing, I've done a draft of the delivery routes. I've mapped three routes covering the target households, with estimated timings of 2-3 hours per route including the doorstep check. I've checked against our current workload and it's feasible if we dedicate one day per week to the pilot. The routes are in T4. I'd like to confirm the weekly schedule—should we do all deliveries on one day or spread them across the week?

Good question. I'd suggest one day per week—it's simpler to manage, easier to coordinate with community partners, and reduces the risk of missed households. Let's say Thursdays. That gives us time to pack on Wednesday and adjust if needed. Does that work for the delivery team?
Thursday works for me. I'll update the routes to reflect that schedule and confirm the final plan by EOD tomorrow. That covers D4.

I'll have the packing test done by Wednesday. Once we've tested and confirmed the process works, I'll draft the packing checklist (T6) and share it for final sign-off. The checklist will cover item types, quantities, expiry checks, and any special handling notes.

Perfect. Once the checklist is done, I'll review it and we can lock in D3. I'll also make sure the food safety guide (A2) is clearly posted and that everyone knows the key rules before we start packing.

Great. So to summarise: we're testing the packing process this week, finalising the collection and sorting process (D3) by end of week, confirming the delivery schedule and routes (D4) by EOD tomorrow, and drafting the packing checklist (A3) by Wednesday. That gives us a solid operational foundation before we move to the safety and privacy thread. Any concerns?

threads.thread_goal: Finalise safety, privacy and doorstep interaction guidelines.

messages.text: I've drafted the food safety and hygiene quick guide (A2) based on standard food handling rules. It covers hand washing, temperature checks, storage rotation, and transport safety. The guide is simple and non-technical so all staff can follow it. I'd like feedback from the team, especially on whether there are any gaps or if anything is unclear. Once we've reviewed, we'll need sign-off for D5.

I've read through A2. It's clear and practical. One thing I'd add—what do we do if we find food that's borderline on expiry or condition? Should there be a simple decision tree or do we just discard it? I want to make sure everyone applies the same standard.
Good point. I'll add a simple rule: if in doubt, discard. We can't risk a food safety incident. I'll update A2 to include that and re-share by EOD today.

Thanks. I've also drafted the doorstep wellbeing and needs-check script (A4) for T5. It's short—just three open questions about how they're managing, any immediate needs, and whether they'd like to be contacted again. The language is non-judgmental and non-clinical. I want to make sure it feels natural and doesn't put staff in an awkward position. Can you all review and let me know if it feels right?

I've reviewed the script. It's good—short and respectful. One thing: I'd suggest adding a note that staff can opt out of the conversation if they're not comfortable, or if the household doesn't want to chat. We don't want anyone feeling pressured. Also, how long should the conversation take? I'm thinking 2-3 minutes max so it doesn't delay the delivery.

Excellent points. I'll add a note about opt-out and time limits. The script should take 2-3 minutes if the household is willing to chat. I'll also make sure the training brief covers how to handle a household that doesn't want to engage—we just leave the food and move on. Let me update A4 and share the final version by tomorrow morning.

I've been thinking about the privacy side. When we record notes from the doorstep conversations, we need to make sure we're not capturing personal identifiers. I'll be setting up the logging templates (T8), and I want to align with you on what information is safe to record. Should we use anonymised household codes instead of names or addresses?

Absolutely. We'll use anonymised codes for all households in the logs. No names, addresses, or personal details in the outreach notes. Just the code, date, and a brief note on what was discussed or any concerns. I'll review the log template with you before it's finalised. For now, let me confirm: A2 will be updated with the 'if in doubt, discard' rule by EOD today, and A4 will be finalised by tomorrow morning. Once both are done, we can sign off on D5 and D6. Sound good?

threads.thread_goal: Set up tracking, labelling and logging tools before the dry run.

messages.text: I've drafted the labelling and coding scheme for T7. The idea is to use a simple format: HH-001, HH-002, etc., for each household. This code goes on the parcel label and in the tracking sheet, but not on any outreach notes. I've also created a tracking sheet template (A5) that records the household code, assigned route, and delivery status each week. Can you review and let me know if this approach works?

The coding scheme is clean and simple. I like it. One thing—we need to keep a separate master list that maps the codes to actual household details, but that list should be stored securely and only accessible to the social work team. The delivery and outreach logs will only use codes. Does that work?

Yes, that makes sense. I'll add a note to the tracking sheet that the master list is confidential and stored separately. Now, for the delivery and outreach log (A6), I've drafted a template with columns for date, route, household code, items delivered, and key notes. The notes section is for brief observations—e.g., 'household seemed well', 'mentioned food allergies', etc. No personal details. Does this feel right?

That's good. I'd add one more column for any concerns or follow-ups needed—e.g., 'household mentioned needing support with benefits', so we can flag that for the social work team to follow up separately. But again, no personal identifiers in the log itself.

Good idea. I'll add that column. So the final template will have: date, route, household code, items delivered, key notes, and follow-up flags. I'll have the full A5 and A6 templates ready by EOD tomorrow, and we can lock in D7 once you've reviewed.
Just to confirm—the household codes will be printed on the parcel labels, right? So when I'm out on delivery, I just match the code on the parcel to the code in my route plan. That's straightforward.
Exactly. The code on the parcel matches the code in the route plan and the tracking sheet. Simple and secure. I'll make sure the label format is clear and easy to read.

Perfect. So D7 is locked in—we're using the HH-001 coding scheme with the tracking sheet and log templates. Once A5 and A6 are finalised by EOD tomorrow, we'll have all the tools we need for the dry run. This is good progress.

threads.thread_goal: Review dry run results and agree adjustments and next steps.

messages.text: We've completed the dry run with 5 households over the past week. Overall, it went well, but we've captured some issues in the operational log (A7). Key findings: packing took longer than expected (about 45 minutes for 5 parcels instead of 30), one household had a dietary restriction we didn't know about, and the doorstep conversations were brief and positive. I've documented the issues and some quick fixes. Let me share the summary and we can discuss what needs to change before the full roll-out.

The packing time is something we flagged in testing. I think the issue is that we're being too careful with the expiry checks. Once we're in a rhythm, it should speed up. But I agree we need to build in a bit more buffer time. Maybe 1 hour for 5 parcels instead of 30 minutes?

That's fair. I'll update the process to allow 1 hour for 5 parcels. For the dietary restriction issue, I think we need to ask community partners to flag any known allergies or restrictions when they give us the household list. That way we can plan the parcels accordingly. I'll add that to the collection process.

The routes worked well. Deliveries took about 2.5 hours for 5 households, which is in line with our estimate. The doorstep conversations were smooth—households were receptive and the script felt natural. No issues there. I'd say we're ready to scale up to the full 15-20 households.

Great feedback. So the adjustments are: allow 1 hour for packing 5 parcels, ask community partners for dietary restrictions upfront, and confirm that the routes and doorstep conversations are working well. I think we're ready for D8—go ahead with the full 6-week roll-out. Does everyone agree?
I've reviewed the logs from the dry run. The tracking and coding system worked smoothly. No issues with the labels or the log templates. I'm ready to move forward.
I'm ready too. The packing process is solid once we adjust the timing. I'll make sure the team knows about the dietary restrictions and the updated timeline.

Excellent. D8 is confirmed—we're going ahead with the full 6-week pilot roll-out starting next week. I'll schedule a brief team briefing (T9) for Monday to cover the objectives, roles, safety and privacy guidelines, and any final questions. I'll also start monitoring weekly metrics and feedback (T11) from week 1 onwards. We'll do a mid-pilot check-in at week 3 to catch any issues early. Sound good?
Perfect. I'll be ready to start deliveries next Thursday with the full household list. Looking forward to it.

Great. Let me summarise the next steps: I'll run the team briefing on Monday (T9), we'll start the full roll-out next Thursday, and I'll post weekly summaries every Monday (T11). At the end of week 3, we'll do a mid-pilot debrief to check in on any issues. And at the end of week 6, I'll compile the final summary report (T12) with recommendations. Everyone clear?
